anchors.name: Dimensional dark skin rendering
anchors.concrete_expression: Render dark skin with dimensional highlight rolloff and meaningful shadow detail and natural texture; never flatten the face into a single exposure value; protect skin tone separation in shadows.

anchors.name: Human dignity ahead of visual gimmickry
anchors.concrete_expression: Frame the person as a full psychological subject at a respectful camera distance, with posture and eye line, dimensional skin rendering and non-exploitative framing, and expressions observed rather than posed; no decorative gimmick separates the person from the scene. Translation of 'dignity' per section 0A lines 111-112, applied with this profile's Composition and camera and Character direction rules, lines 255-268.

anchors.name: Environment communicates social context
anchors.concrete_expression: The environment visibly communicates social position, institutional pressure, family structure or community context: a socially meaningful, lived-in location (street, home, public building, courtroom, classroom, transit space or gathering place) with relationships and power revealed by group blocking; where institutional pressure is meant, rigid architecture, authority figures controlling foreground space, compressed blocking or restrictive sightlines. Translation per section 0A lines 111-112 and this profile's invariants and Texture and environment rules, lines 244-265.

anchors.name: Controlled camera movement: still observation to fluid emotional attachment
anchors.concrete_expression: Use controlled camera movement that can shift between still observation and fluid emotional attachment.

anchors.name: Naturalistic or plausibly motivated light
anchors.concrete_expression: Favor naturalistic or plausibly motivated light even when the result is visually rich: a named in-scene source (window, practical lamp, overcast daylight, late sun or institutional fixture) appears to be the reason the scene is lit, soft but directional, with shadow carrying emotional weight without erasing facial information.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Controlled camera movement: still observation to fluid emotional attachment
uncheckable_by_design.reason: A shift between still observation and fluid attachment is a motion/sequence property. A single still image and its compiled prompt can encode one mode, not the shift between modes, so no prompt token can verify this anchor as written. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.concrete_expression: Stage the impossible event as documentary reality: vehicles, bodies, buildings, water, smoke and debris carry believable mass and inertia, extraordinary motion creates environmental consequences, and if physics is violated in the event, everything else in the frame obeys physics; the strangeness lives in the event, never in decorative photography.
anchors.name: Extraordinary events are treated as physical reality

anchors.concrete_expression: Every major light source is physically plausible and named in the scene (sky, window, practical lamp, headlights, fluorescent fixture, fire, projection, industrial light); no gratuitous rim light and no fantasy glow.
anchors.name: Lighting looks motivated by the environment rather than by decorative movie lighting

anchors.concrete_expression: Roads, corridors, bridges, stairwells, windows, runways, city blocks, laboratories, machinery and institutional spaces create strong horizontals, verticals, rectangles and vanishing lines; the geometry feels structural, not decorative.
anchors.name: Architecture and infrastructure create strong functional geometry

anchors.concrete_expression: The camera sits at a human-scale, observational position (standing or seated eye height within the space) so the impossible event reads as something a person present could witness, combining intimate human proximity with the larger system around it.
anchors.name: Human-scale camera positions make impossible events feel observable and real

anchors.concrete_expression: Even in close images, architecture or environmental force remains present and readable around the face; naturalistic wide-to-normal perspective keeps enough background information to understand the space, with no default portrait-mode bokeh.
anchors.name: Environmental information remains important even in close portraiture

anchors.concrete_expression: The neighborhood stays legible and meaningful around the subject: signs, walls, murals, storefronts, flags and crowds carry meaning inside the frame, and ensemble blocking and crowd geography visibly encode alliances, factions and tensions.

anchors.concrete_expression: Bold color is assigned to objects and factions (wardrobe, painted walls, signs, food stands, vehicles, brick, asphalt, sunlight) rather than added as global saturation; in heat-driven scenes warm surfaces and red/orange accents with hard sun raise the emotional temperature.
anchors.name: Color can operate as emotional temperature or political pressure

anchors.concrete_expression: Wide-to-normal focal lengths at close physical distance, with perspective exaggeration increasing the emotional charge while the environment behind the character stays legible.
anchors.name: Wide lenses frequently place characters close to the viewer while preserving neighborhood context

anchors.concrete_expression: Low-angle hero or confrontation frames, canted frames and exaggerated proximity appear when tension or a heightened psychological state motivates them, never as random decoration.
anchors.name: Perspective may become aggressive through low angles, canted frames, or exaggerated proximity

anchors.name: Production design and costume color-planned as a unified system

anchors.concrete_expression: In a still, the gliding reveal is expressed as layered threshold framing: arches, doorways, circular motifs, layers and foreground objects arranged so the viewer feels they have just discovered the subject through a threshold, connecting the character to the architecture.

anchors.name: Memory is warm and specific rather than hazy and generic
anchors.concrete_expression: Make memory warm and specific rather than hazy and generic: particular people, rooms and objects carrying character history (books, clothes, wallpaper, dishes, furniture, school spaces, bedrooms) in warm natural color, with no generic haze standing in for recollection.

anchors.name: Grain and slight optical imperfection help the image feel lived rather than digitally pristine

anchors.name: Group blocking matters: families and friends overlap, interrupt, touch, and share frames

anchors.name: Youth may produce looser, more kinetic camera behavior; adulthood or separation may become more composed
anchors.concrete_expression: Match camera behavior to the scene's emotional time: buoyant, close, mobile handling for youth or joy, and more measured, composed framing where maturity or separation has entered. A single still encodes the one behavior its moment calls for.

anchors.name: Light tracks identity and emotional state
anchors.concrete_expression: Let light track identity and emotional state: the character's placement in shadow, color or openness shifts with their psychological state, including a conceptual move from shadow toward light when the story calls for liberation or clarity.

anchors.name: Darkness is expressive but should retain dimensional skin information
anchors.concrete_expression: Keep darkness expressive without erasing the face: shadow remains visible as shadow while highlights on cheekbones, forehead, nose, eyes and lips model the skin dimensionally, never crushed into unreadable black.

anchors.name: Camera style follows character rather than a preset 'cool' visual package

anchors.name: Natural locations and historical materials are treated tactically and texturally
anchors.concrete_expression: Treat natural locations and historical materials with tactile, textural attention: weathered earth, wood, cloth and period surfaces kept tactile and lived-in, never spotless or polished. anchors.name: Skin tone, clothing, earth, wood, weather, and practical sources create palette
anchors.concrete_expression: Build the palette from the world: skin tone, clothing, earth, wood, weather and practical sources supply the colors, with strong environment color striking skin naturally in contemporary interiors and earth, wood, faded cotton, warm highlights and blue-black shadow in historical or rural settings.

anchors.name: Darkness is a place, not simply low exposure

anchors.name: Curtains, doorways, hallways, closets, stages, bedrooms, lamps, clubs, and empty roads become thresholds

anchors.name: Saturated primary color, especially red, can function as an emotional alarm
anchors.concrete_expression: Use saturated primary color, especially red, as an emotional alarm: a selective strong red (with browns, yellows or deep blue-black) placed where the feeling spikes, never an all-over neon wash.

anchors.name: Pools of practical light may float inside large areas of black
anchors.concrete_expression: Float isolated pools of practical light inside large areas of black: table lamps, sconces, headlights, stage light, neon or weak daylight as islands, with surrounding rooms falling nearly black.

anchors.name: Street and neighborhood identity remain visible around characters
anchors.concrete_expression: Keep street and neighborhood identity visible around the characters: specific blocks, signs, porches, cars, clubs, studios and houses stay readable as social spaces, never blurred into an anonymous backdrop.

anchors.name: Camera movement carries performance energy and urban momentum
anchors.concrete_expression: Give the camera performance energy and urban momentum: street-level, shoulder-height perspective in moving proximity with moderate wide lenses, the viewer physically near the group or vehicle as it travels. Still residue of this profile's Camera rule (moving camera, readable action geography).

anchors.name: Handheld or documentary-style responsiveness is acceptable when it increases authenticity
anchors.concrete_expression: Allow handheld or documentary-style responsiveness where it increases authenticity: reactive framing that follows the action as it happens rather than pre-composed or over-stabilized polish.

anchors.name: Practical color temperatures — sodium orange, fluorescent green, cool night, warm interiors — can coexist
anchors.concrete_expression: Let practical color temperatures coexist without neutralization: sodium orange street light against cooler ambient night, fluorescent green interiors against warm skin, sun-baked afternoon against dark car interiors, kept in real conflict in the same scene.

anchors.name: Optical or textural imperfection prevents the image from feeling sterile
anchors.concrete_expression: Keep optical and textural imperfection in the image: grain, older-lens softness, flare, slight halation, atmospheric haze, scuffed vehicles, worn asphalt, sweat and smoke, so the scene never feels sterile.

anchors.name: Camera perspective is organized around subjective bodily experience
anchors.concrete_expression: Organize the camera around subjective bodily experience: perspective attached to the protagonist's body and sensation, so the viewer is trapped inside the physical and mental loop rather than watching it from outside.

anchors.name: Repetition of actions/objects can become a visual ritual
anchors.concrete_expression: Turn repetition into visual ritual: 2-4 repeated sensory details tied to the obsession recur across the composition, with at least one close symbolic detail included, or a repetitive ritual implied through objects and body posture. Translation for stills per this profile's Detail system rule, line 1920.

anchors.name: Extreme close detail — eye, hand, pill, needle, skin, food, mirror, wound, fabric — can compress the world into obsession
anchors.concrete_expression: Compress the world into obsession through extreme close detail: one macro-scale detail (eye, hand, pill, needle, skin, food, mirror, wound or fabric) carries the psychological weight of the scene.

anchors.name: Wide lenses used close to the body increase distortion and pressure
anchors.concrete_expression: Use wide lenses close to the body so distortion and pressure rise: over-close wide-angle proximity bends the space around the subject and increases psychological pressure.

anchors.name: Attached/body-mounted perspective can make the background move unnaturally around a stable face
anchors.concrete_expression: Use attached, body-mounted perspective: the face stays stable and fixed while the background geometry feels unstable and moves unnaturally around it. Still translation per this profile's Camera rule: background geometry can feel unstable while the subject remains fixed.

anchors.name: Period beauty is organized around social power and identity
anchors.concrete_expression: Organize period beauty around social power and identity: body placement, architecture and costume show who belongs, who is being displayed and who is being excluded inside the rigid social system.

anchors.name: Color palettes can distinguish families, institutions, countries, or emotional climates
anchors.concrete_expression: Give competing social worlds distinct palette families tied to rooms, costumes, upholstery and daylight rather than grading alone: for example cold powder blue and silver for an emotionally restrictive aristocratic space against warm gold, ochre and cream for intimacy or security.

anchors.name: Classical rooms, portraits, staircases, gardens, dining tables, and formal dress become power geometry
anchors.concrete_expression: Make classical rooms, portraits, staircases, gardens, dining tables and formal dress into power geometry: balanced classical framing, doorways, long tables, portrait walls and garden axes, with carefully spaced bodies whose placement reveals rank and exclusion.

anchors.name: Dark skin should remain luminous inside historically styled interiors and exteriors
anchors.concrete_expression: Keep dark skin luminous inside historically styled interiors and exteriors: window daylight, candles, fireplaces, overcast exterior light or soft directional period light preserving facial dimensionality across varied skin tones, never overexposed or dulled.

anchors.name: Composition is elegant and controlled but character perspective remains central
anchors.concrete_expression: Keep composition elegant and controlled while character perspective remains central: the balanced classical frame serves what the character experiences and where they stand in the hierarchy, not museum-like stiffness.

anchors.name: Time may feel stretched, skipped, repeated, or smeared
anchors.concrete_expression: Make time feel stretched, repeated or smeared inside the still: selective motion smear around a relatively stable subject, repeated reflections, rain streaks, passing bodies, clocks or layered foreground suggesting time sliding rather than freezing. Translation per this profile's Time/motion in a still rule, line 2138.

anchors.name: Characters are often physically close but architecturally separated
anchors.concrete_expression: Keep characters physically close but architecturally separated: doorways, mirrors, glass, curtains or narrow corridors divide people who are near each other, so closeness and separation read in the same frame.

anchors.name: Foreground objects, doorframes, mirrors, glass, curtains, and narrow passageways create partial views
anchors.concrete_expression: Create partial views: a wall, doorway, mirror edge, window, shelf, passerby or curtain occupies significant foreground, and characters are placed in narrow restaurants, stairwells, hotel corridors, apartments, alleys, trains or night streets.

anchors.name: Practical neon, tungsten, fluorescent, street color, or deep red/green can carry emotion
anchors.concrete_expression: Let practical color carry the emotion: neon, tungsten, fluorescent, street color or deep red/green built from named in-scene sources (green fluorescent, red wall, amber lamp, cyan sign, sodium street light, patterned dress), with one or two colors dominating the scene emotionally.

anchors.name: Wide lenses used close can distort intimate urban interiors
anchors.concrete_expression: Use wide-to-normal lenses close to faces in tight urban interiors, allowing edge distortion when it intensifies intimacy; no clean commercial portrait distance.

CIS-18.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 2109-2215).

anchors.name: Action should feel physically consequential and spatially understandable
anchors.concrete_expression: Stage action whose physical consequences are visible (fatigue, injury, damage, effort) inside geography the viewer can map: readable threat direction, clear entry and exit paths, and space established objectively before pressure closes in.

anchors.name: Camera distance can change to reflect a protagonist's mental state
anchors.concrete_expression: For a single still, choose the camera distance that matches the psychological intensity of the moment: observational distance while geography is established, physically closer, lower or more reactive framing as danger becomes personal. Translation per this profile's Camera rule, line 2238.

anchors.name: Hard daylight, mixed urban night, fluorescent interiors, and practical sources contribute grit
anchors.concrete_expression: Light the scene from the profile's practical register (hard sun, window shafts, sodium/LED street sources, fluorescent institutional light, vehicle headlights, fire or practical lamps), allowing mixed temperatures and controlled shadow so the light itself carries grit.

anchors.name: Faces are often photographed under moral or physical pressure rather than glamour
anchors.concrete_expression: Photograph faces under moral or physical pressure: tense, fatigued, morally charged expressions lit by the scene's hard practical sources, never glamour-lit.

anchors.name: Sweat, grime, smoke, rain, glass, metal, asphalt, gym texture, or weapon surfaces carry material weight
anchors.concrete_expression: Give the listed materials tactile weight in the frame (sweat, grime, smoke, rain, glass, metal, asphalt, gym texture or weapon surfaces), preserving bruises, fabric strain, chipped paint, cracked pavement and dust rather than clean action-figure surfaces.

uncheckable_by_design.reason: The anchor's core property is a change of camera distance across a sequence as mental state shifts. anchors.name: Very wide lenses used close to subjects distort rooms and social relationships
anchors.concrete_expression: Use an extreme wide lens close to the subject so faces, hands, furniture, corridors or ceilings stretch perceptually and the room itself distorts the social relationship.

anchors.name: Large spaces can make people look lonely, absurd, or institutionally trapped
anchors.concrete_expression: Place small, isolated figures inside oversized rooms and long visual axes with large pockets of empty space, so scale itself makes them look lonely, absurd or institutionally trapped.

anchors.name: Camera positions may be too high, too low, too far, or geometrically unexpected
anchors.concrete_expression: Choose a camera position that is too high, too low, too far or geometrically unexpected for conventional coverage, so the viewpoint itself is destabilizing.

anchors.name: Natural/available light often coexists with lavish production design
anchors.concrete_expression: Light with natural or practical sources (windows, candles, daylight, overcast sky, practical fixtures) inside lavish, elaborate production design, letting available light and designed opulence coexist.

anchors.name: Long, fluid moves replace conventional shot/reverse-shot coverage
anchors.concrete_expression: Long, fluid moves replace conventional shot/reverse-shot coverage.

anchors.name: The neighborhood is a social system, not a generic urban backdrop
anchors.concrete_expression: Build the neighborhood as a readable social system: streets, porches, yards, cars, fences, homes, schools and signs carry social meaning (pressure, surveillance, family, history) around the people, never an anonymous backdrop.

anchors.name: Foreground objects, signs, fences, aircraft, cars, and street layouts can carry thematic meaning
anchors.concrete_expression: Give foreground objects thematic work: signs, fences, aircraft, cars and street layouts, plus one environmental detail that quietly reveals pressure or history (a sign, police cruiser, distant plane, fence, memorial, boarded building or family object).

anchors.name: Family interiors and porches are intimate counterspaces to public danger
anchors.concrete_expression: Use family interiors and porches as intimate counterspaces: inhabited domestic warmth and group life set against the public danger of the street outside.

anchors.name: Camera behavior is usually observational until emotion or violence destabilizes it
anchors.concrete_expression: Hold an observational, relational camera for the still: eye-level or slightly low street perspective and medium-wide relational framing with ordinary geography clear; only when the depicted moment is one of broken social control, move closer or rougher. Translation per this profile's Camera rule, line 2452.

anchors.name: Natural daylight, practical night sources, and location texture preserve realism
anchors.concrete_expression: Use natural daylight and practical night sources (sun, shade, porch light, streetlamp, car light, kitchen light, school fluorescent) and preserve location texture so color belongs to the chosen environment.

anchors.name: Architecture encodes class, access, privacy, labor, and power
anchors.concrete_expression: Design the architecture to encode class, access, privacy, labor and power: who is above whom, who can see outside, who must descend, who controls the doorway, who occupies the clean open plane and who is compressed under objects or ceilings.

anchors.name: Vertical movement — stairs, hills, basements, elevated rooms — frequently carries social meaning
anchors.concrete_expression: Use vertical elements (stairs, hills, basements, elevated rooms) so a figure's height, ascent or descent in the frame itself carries social meaning.

anchors.name: Windows, doors, tunnels, platforms, and corridors act as frames within frames
anchors.concrete_expression: Compose with windows, doors, tunnels, platforms and corridors as frames within frames, so architecture nests the figures and diagrams their relationships.

anchors.name: Blocking is precise enough that relationships can be understood without dialogue
anchors.concrete_expression: Block characters precisely (levels, distances, who faces whom, who is separated by glass, stairs or thresholds) so the social relationship is visible before any dialogue.

anchors.name: Background action is often important; deep or moderate focus preserves it
anchors.concrete_expression: Keep deep or moderate focus so background action stays legible and important; do not isolate subjects with shallow focus.

anchors.name: Family space can feel loving, secretive, haunted, and sensuous at once
anchors.concrete_expression: Build the family space from concrete carriers of the four registers at once: a layered family tableau in a warm amber interior (loving, sensuous), partially concealed observation and layered doorways (secretive), and mirrors, reflections or stillness that let the supernatural overlap the real (haunted).

anchors.name: Southern landscape and weather carry memory
anchors.concrete_expression: Let Southern landscape and weather carry memory: bayou water, moss, trees, fields and humid air treated as memory space around the family, not scenery.

anchors.name: Mirrors, water, windows, reflections, photographs, and visions can bridge reality and memory
anchors.concrete_expression: Bridge reality and memory with a reflective or photographic device inside the scene (mirror, water, window, reflection or family photograph) through which a vision or remembered presence enters, photographically continuous with the surrounding world.

anchors.name: Warm amber/brown interior light contrasts with humid green/blue exterior space
anchors.concrete_expression: Contrast warm amber/brown interior light (window light, candles, lamps) against humid green/blue exterior atmosphere (dusk, moonlight, sun filtered through trees).

anchors.name: Children or emotionally vulnerable observers may organize the point of view
anchors.concrete_expression: Organize the point of view through a child or emotionally vulnerable observer: a child-height or intimate observer's perspective that makes adult spaces feel charged.

anchors.name: Monumental architecture or landscape often dwarfs the human figure
anchors.concrete_expression: Make monumental architecture or landscape dwarf the human figure: enormous walls, voids, deserts, mountains, brutalist rooms or vast skies, with the person smaller than conventional hero framing when scale is the story.

anchors.name: Negative space is a primary compositional tool
anchors.concrete_expression: Use negative space as a primary compositional tool: large uninterrupted shapes and clean horizon lines leave most of the frame empty around a small, precisely placed figure.

anchors.name: Camera movement is generally deliberate, not frenetic
anchors.concrete_expression: Give the still a deliberate, calm camera logic: restrained wide or normal perspective, a slow push/pull feeling and clear spatial hierarchy, with no frenetic action-camera energy. Translation per this profile's Camera/lens rule, line 2779.

anchors.name: Atmosphere — fog, dust, rain, snow, smoke, heat, darkness — shapes depth
anchors.concrete_expression: Let one atmospheric condition (fog, dust, rain, snow, smoke, heat or darkness) shape the depth of the scene, graded by distance rather than added as decoration.

anchors.name: Lighting often feels like one dominant source or environmental condition
anchors.concrete_expression: Light the whole scene from one dominant environmental source or condition (overcast sky, low sun, fog-diffused daylight, orange dust light, cold artificial ceiling, hard desert sun or deep night practicals); do not light objects independently.

anchors.name: Everyday environments are shown directly rather than exoticized
anchors.concrete_expression: Show everyday environments directly: gates, offices, courtyards, markets, houses and streets presented as ordinary social stages, with no exoticizing grade or tourist framing.

anchors.name: Symbolic objects emerge from normal life rather than floating as abstract metaphors
anchors.concrete_expression: Let one ordinary, culturally grounded object (mask, bowl, letter, stamp, garment, vehicle, sign, chair or radio) gather symbolic meaning from who handles it and where it appears inside normal life.

anchors.name: Frontal, clear, often relatively deep compositions support social legibility
anchors.concrete_expression: Use frontal, clear, relatively deep compositions so the social arrangement (who sits, stands, waits, serves, commands, enters or is excluded) reads immediately.

anchors.name: Groups and public space matter as much as individual psychological portraiture
anchors.concrete_expression: Stage groups in public space with the same weight as any individual portrait: community groups engaged in work, ritual, trade, argument or waiting, not glamorous isolation.

anchors.name: Costume and color can identify social role, tradition, bureaucracy, or contradiction
anchors.concrete_expression: Let costume and culturally specific color identify social role, tradition, bureaucracy or contradiction (uniforms, garments, signage and textile color read as social information).

anchors.name: Color embedded in objects before grading
anchors.concrete_expression: Color is embedded in wardrobe, walls, furniture, art, food, flowers and objects before grading: 3-5 principal colors with strong separation assigned to actual surfaces (wall, sofa, dress, phone, flower, curtain, kitchen tile, artwork), not a saturation of the entire image.

anchors.name: Intensely separated principal colors
anchors.concrete_expression: Reds, blues, yellows, greens, black and cream may be intensely separated as the principal color family.

anchors.name: Readable, emotionally significant backgrounds
anchors.concrete_expression: Backgrounds remain readable and emotionally significant: enough background focus that the room contributes to the emotion rather than the subject being blurred away from it.

anchors.name: Graphic, sensual, character-specific domestic interiors
anchors.concrete_expression: Domestic interiors are graphic, sensual and character-specific, treated as designed emotional diagrams using doorways, mirrors, tables, beds, kitchens, corridors and art as structured graphic elements.

anchors.name: Painterly, contrasty light with real skin
anchors.concrete_expression: Light can be painterly and contrasty while skin remains flattering but real, using windows, lamps, practicals, daylight and painterly directional sources, preserving color integrity.

anchors.name: Rough location realism and psychedelic abstraction coexist
anchors.concrete_expression: Hold rough location realism and psychedelic abstraction in one frame: a believable street location with grain and imperfect framing, fractured by a strong color or superimposition event.

anchors.name: Jump cuts, superimpositions, repeated frames, and abrupt montage can express urgency
anchors.concrete_expression: Express urgency inside the single frame with the profile's still-form disruptions: superimposed figures, repeated body positions, motion echo or jump-cut-like temporal layering over the location base. Translation per this profile's Collage layer and Rhythm in a still rules, lines 3095 and 3101.

anchors.name: Strong monochromatic colorization or neon-like fields may represent psychological distance
anchors.concrete_expression: Use strong monochromatic colorization (a red, yellow or blue wash) or neon-like fields as a structural event over part of the frame, with ordinary color returning around it.

anchors.name: Street texture remains visible beneath experimentation
anchors.concrete_expression: Keep street grain, hard light and imperfect framing visible beneath every collage intervention; never smooth the base location away.

anchors.name: Zooms, freeze-like moments, optical printing, and layered exposure are valid tools
anchors.concrete_expression: Use the still forms of the profile's optical tools: zoom energy, a freeze-like arrested moment, posterized optical-print texture and layered exposure inside the single frame.

anchors.name: Walking, wandering, and tracking create discovery
anchors.concrete_expression: Eye-level walking perspective with a gentle tracking feeling and handheld observation: the subject is encountered mid-walk at human scale in a real street, room, beach or market, as if discovered while moving rather than posed for the camera. Translation per the profile's Camera rule, line 3199.

anchors.name: Documentary observation can sit beside constructed tableaux, intertitles, color devices, or staged images
anchors.concrete_expression: A documentary-observed scene carries one deliberate formal intervention from the profile's formal-play vocabulary (a framed photograph within the scene, a color-to-monochrome division, a handwritten sign, a mirrored duplicate, a playful scale contrast, or a staged tableau inside documentary reality) without the intervention cancelling the realism around it.

anchors.name: Mirrors, shop windows, photographs, posters, and reflective surfaces complicate identity
anchors.concrete_expression: A mirror, shop window, photograph, poster or other reflective surface inside the scene doubles or fragments the subject's identity: a reflection, a pictured face, or a poster figure rhymes with or contradicts the real person.

anchors.name: Small objects and overlooked people receive visual attention
anchors.concrete_expression: A small overlooked subject (a hand, an old wall, a sign, hair, an abandoned object, a passerby, a market display, beach debris) receives deliberate visual attention and is built into a visual rhyme with the main subject instead of serving as background decoration.

anchors.name: The filmmaker's own curiosity or presence can be acknowledged rather than hidden
anchors.concrete_expression: The image-maker's presence is acknowledged inside the frame: a hand entering the shot, the photographer's shadow or reflection caught in a mirror, or a subject's direct acknowledging look into the lens, so curiosity stays visible rather than hidden behind neutrality.

anchors.name: Multiple media textures can coexist inside one project
anchors.concrete_expression: Visibly different media languages coexist and their difference stays legible: two or more explicit media from the profile's media vocabulary (16mm narrative texture, consumer VHS/Hi8 video, black-and-white archival still, photocopy, library record, interview frame) sit side by side in the frame or its layers with grain, tape softness and wear intact. Per the Media selection rule, line 3306: if combining layers, make the difference visible.

anchors.name: Direct address and talking-head framing create intimacy and self-awareness
anchors.concrete_expression: The subject addresses the camera directly in a talking-head or interview framing: face to lens, a simple interview setup, a casual handheld interior behind them, so the image knows it is being recorded.

anchors.name: Staged archival material may be intentionally credible but slightly uncanny
anchors.concrete_expression: A staged black-and-white archival image made materially plausible rather than spectacular: period clothing, monochrome silver-gelatin feel, age marks, simple studio or location posing, credible enough to pass as found history with a slight uncanny edge. Per the Archive rule, line 3312.

anchors.name: Domestic, retail, street, library, bar, and community spaces retain low-budget immediacy
anchors.concrete_expression: The setting is an unpolished domestic, retail, street, library, bar or community space shot with casual handheld immediacy: shelves, records, photographs, apartments and stores kept as found, with no prestige lighting or production gloss.

anchors.name: Fiction and documentary evidence can deliberately contaminate one another
anchors.concrete_expression: Fiction and documentary deliberately contaminate each other in one frame: a staged or invented archival photograph is handled as evidence inside a documentary scene of searching, recording or cataloguing, so the categories visibly leak into one another.

CIS-29.micro_rules_source: No numeric micro-rule is stated in this profile (checked in full, lines 3286-3392); the medium names (16mm, VHS/Hi8) are media selections, not numeric rules, and no value was invented.

avoid.text: cleaning every medium into one modern look
fake VHS overlays that do not affect image behavior
treating queer life as an exotic subject

CIS-29.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 3286-3392).

anchors.name: Handheld reactivity, zooms, reframing, and imperfect timing can make performance feel unprotected
anchors.concrete_expression: Raw-proximity mode: handheld-feeling eye level, imperfect centering, rough exposure and faces caught mid-action with visible motion, so the performance looks unprotected rather than covered. Translation per the profile's Mode A rule, line 3413, which is the profile's own conversion of reactivity into a still.

anchors.name: Natural/practical light may be accepted even when unflattering
anchors.concrete_expression: Available natural or practical light is accepted as found, even when it is unflattering: no beautifying fill or corrective polish is imposed on the face.

anchors.name: Cutting or framing can feel rough instead of smoothing emotion into classical coverage
anchors.concrete_expression: Framing stays rough: imperfect centering, abrupt crops and reframed compositions that refuse to smooth the emotion into classical coverage.

anchors.name: Iconic tableaux appear as a contrasting mode, not the constant baseline
anchors.concrete_expression: Where the sublime-tableau mode is used, it lands as a contrast inside the friction system: one dominant image mode with a single element from the opposite mode intruding, per the Friction rule, line 3419, instead of the image settling into tableau as its baseline.

anchors.name: Grand landscapes, bodies, animals, weather, or celestial imagery may become symbolic
anchors.concrete_expression: A grand landscape, body, animal, weather system or celestial image is composed to carry symbolic weight against the human subject, with an emotional contradiction inside it rather than decorative grandeur.

micro_rules_source.opposite_mode_intrusions: section 30, Friction rule, line 3419: 'Do not mix both modes into mush. Choose one as the dominant image mode, then allow one element from the other to intrude.'

avoid.text: symbolic imagery with no emotional contradiction

CIS-30.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 3393-3499). Mode B's grand landscapes and painterly composition do not state spacious framing as such.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Handheld reactivity, zooms, reframing, and imperfect timing can make performance feel unprotected
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Reactivity and imperfect timing are temporal performance properties: a single still can show only their residue (imperfect centering, a face caught mid-action, visible motion), and whether the performance 'feels unprotected' is an emotional-quality judgment no token can settle. The anchor record carries the Mode A stills translation; the timing element itself is residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Iconic tableaux appear as a contrasting mode, not the constant baseline
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Whether tableaux are the constant baseline is a property of a body of images, not of one still. A single image can encode the friction rule (one dominant mode, one intruding element), which the anchor record does, but it cannot evidence the cross-project half of the anchor. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.name: Camera height and angle carry political and psychological power
anchors.concrete_expression: Camera height is chosen as a power statement per the Point-of-view rule, line 3520: low angle when a marginalized subject must acquire visual sovereignty, high angle when a system is suppressing or surveilling, eye level when witness and equality are required; never an angle chosen for coolness.

anchors.name: History, memory, present time, and ancestral consciousness may coexist nonlinearly
anchors.concrete_expression: Temporal layers coexist in one frame through exactly one visual bridge from the profile's bridge vocabulary (repeated body position, ancestral object, landscape match, double-exposure feeling, archival texture, shadow, doorway, or costume echo), suggesting historical presence without generic ghost effects. Per the Time/memory rule, line 3523.

anchors.name: Faces are often confronted directly and given moral weight
anchors.concrete_expression: A frontal face confronts the camera directly and is given compositional and moral weight: frontal portraiture, direct gaze, stark face modeling under hard light.

anchors.name: Landscape is historical ground rather than scenery
anchors.concrete_expression: The landscape carries history rather than decorating the frame: historically charged land, roads, fields or historical architecture that the subject's history has passed through, with geography given real compositional weight.

anchors.name: High contrast, grain, earth color, and strong silhouettes are legitimate expressive tools
anchors.concrete_expression: Hard contrast, deep blacks, tactile grain, earth-based color and strong silhouettes are used deliberately as expressive tools, in monochrome or in earth color, and are not corrected away.

micro_rules_source.temporal_bridge_count: section 31, Time/memory, line 3523: 'Use one visual bridge between temporal layers: repeated body position, ancestral object, landscape match, double exposure feeling, archival texture, shadow, doorway, or costume echo.'

avoid.text: visual hierarchy that automatically centers institutional power

CIS-31.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 3500-3606). Frontal faces are mandated, but centered composition as such is not stated (CIS-38 discipline).

anchors.name: Camera placement feels exact, deliberate, and repeatable
anchors.concrete_expression: Camera placement is exact and deliberate: stable normal-to-moderately-wide perspective, exact horizontals and verticals, controlled headroom and clean room geometry, as if the position could be repeated to the centimeter.

anchors.name: Movement is smooth, motivated, and mechanically precise when movement is required
anchors.concrete_expression: Where movement is implied, it reads as an exact dolly, stabilized track or impossible-but-perfect camera pass rather than handheld drift. Translation per the profile's Camera/lens rule, line 3630.

anchors.name: Low-key light often comes from plausible practical/environmental sources
anchors.concrete_expression: Low-key light comes only from plausible practical or environmental sources named in the scene (practical lamps, computer screens, windows, fluorescent fixtures, street light, overcast sky, ceiling sources), with blacks clean, shadows controlled and highlights disciplined.

anchors.name: Color is limited, controlled, and integrated with set/costume design
anchors.concrete_expression: Color is limited to the profile's controlled family (cyan-gray, sickly green, nicotine yellow, brown, steel, black, muted flesh) and integrated across set, costume and props, so a warmer or brighter color becomes meaningful because it is rare.

anchors.name: Micro-details of objects, screens, tools, paperwork, wounds, mechanisms, or routines are narratively important
anchors.concrete_expression: One precise procedural micro-detail from the profile's detail vocabulary (typed page, fingerprint, file folder, screen, tool, coffee stain, instrument, cable, weapon component, notebook, or a hand performing a specific task) is placed so that it carries narrative weight.

micro_rules_source.procedural_detail_count: section 32, Detail rule, line 3639: 'Include one precise procedural detail: typed page, fingerprint, file folder, screen, tool, coffee stain, instrument, cable, weapon component, notebook, or hand performing a specific task.'

centered composition.text: 'Use exact horizontals and verticals, controlled headroom, deliberate negative space, centered or carefully offset subjects, clean room geometry'

CIS-32.declared_traits_note: Centered composition is declared because the Composition rule states centered subjects as one of the profile's two sanctioned subject placements (line 3627). The same rule's 'deliberate negative space' was NOT declared as sparse negative space: here negative space is a precision spacing device inside controlled geometry, not sparseness (compare CIS-05, batch 1). Spacious framing and uniform ratio are not mandated (checked in full, lines 3607-3717).

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Movement is smooth, motivated, and mechanically precise when movement is required
uncheckable_by_design.reason: The anchor is conditional: it governs movement only 'when movement is required.' A still with no implied movement cannot encode movement quality at all, and smoothness of motion is a temporal property; the anchor record carries the profile's stills translation (exact dolly / stabilized track feel) for images that do imply movement. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6 (compare CIS-35's conditional anchor).

anchors.name: Observation precedes aesthetic display
anchors.concrete_expression: The camera is set where a patient witness might stand (kitchen doorway, yard edge, sidewalk, window, alley, living room corner, workplace, stairwell) and observes the scene as found, keeping ordinary clutter and household evidence rather than staging a display.

anchors.name: Available/minimal light and modest film texture are accepted rather than overcorrected
anchors.concrete_expression: Available light from the profile's own sources (window light, bare bulbs, porch light, exterior sun/shade, practical kitchen or living-room sources) and a modest 16mm-like grain with occasional exposure imperfection are accepted as they are, not fixed into studio perfection.

anchors.name: Static or gently composed frames let behavior develop naturally
anchors.concrete_expression: A static or gently composed human-height frame lets behavior happen inside it: bodies enter and leave naturally and gestures are caught unposed (work, waiting, play, fatigue, quiet affection), with no performance poses.

anchors.name: Children and adults inhabit the same social world without sentimental separation
anchors.concrete_expression: Children and adults share one frame and one social world with the same visual importance: no sentimental separation and no child posed apart as a symbol, with labor, play and family ritual binding them.

anchors.name: Everyday objects and labor can become lyrical through attention
anchors.concrete_expression: An everyday object or act of labor (laundry, tools, dishes, toys, furniture, a small household gesture) is given the frame's attentive weight until it turns lyrical, without decorative lighting or posing doing the work.

CIS-33.micro_rules_source: No numeric micro-rule is stated in this profile (checked in full, lines 3718-3824); the '16mm-like grain' of the Texture rule (line 3744) is a texture descriptor, not a numeric rule, and no value was invented.
CIS-33.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 3718-3824). Static, gently composed frames do not state spacious framing as such.

anchors.name: Camera behaves like an embedded witness rather than an omniscient action machine
anchors.concrete_expression: The camera sits inside the event as an embedded witness: shoulder-height or long-lens observation from within the space, horizon and geography believable, reacting to the action rather than surveying it omnisciently.

anchors.name: Multiple observational positions may coexist: long lens, shoulder camera, vehicle mount, wide situational view
anchors.concrete_expression: The frame adopts one observational position from the profile's position vocabulary (long lens, shoulder camera, vehicle mount, wide situational view) as one of several simultaneous documentary positions covering the event, with geography open enough that the other positions make sense.

anchors.name: Action spaces remain operationally understandable
anchors.concrete_expression: Enough street, room, vehicle, field, corridor, crowd or compound is shown to understand the operational problem, with obstacles and possible threats positioned clearly; the geography never becomes impossible.

anchors.name: Natural light, dust, heat, darkness, practical sources, and atmospheric conditions are accepted as part of the event
anchors.concrete_expression: The environment leads the light (hard sun, dusty haze, overcast, weak practical night, vehicle headlights, fluorescent interiors, fire, flashlight) and dust, heat and darkness stay in the image as part of the event; no beauty lighting is imposed.

anchors.name: Actors must be able to move through space without waiting for perfect marks
anchors.concrete_expression: Figures move freely through a scene-lit 360-degree space, caught mid-procedure with plausible body mechanics (hands gripping tools plausibly, protective gear affecting posture) instead of posed on marks.

CIS-34.micro_rules_source: No numeric micro-rule is stated in this profile (checked in full, lines 3825-3932); '360-degree' names a spatial working method, not a countable image rule, and no value was invented.

vocabularies_source.observational_positions: section 34, anchor 2, line 3872 (position set restated in the Camera rule, line 3848)

CIS-34.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 3825-3932). The wide situational view serves operational legibility; spacious framing as such is not stated.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Multiple observational positions may coexist: long lens, shoulder camera, vehicle mount, wide situational view
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Coexistence of several camera positions is a coverage property across moments and images; a single still is necessarily taken from one position. The anchor record encodes the per-image half (one true observational position, in geography that supports the others); simultaneity itself cannot be token-verified. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Actors must be able to move through space without waiting for perfect marks
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Freedom from marks is a production-process property (scene lighting and blocking while shooting). A still can show its residue (unposed mid-movement bodies, procedure-true posture), which the anchor record encodes, but cannot evidence how the space was worked. Process trait, residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.name: Wide or medium-wide respectful distance
anchors.concrete_expression: Wide or medium-wide distance respects people and place: people placed as meaningful figures within the environment rather than filling the image with faces, at patient eye-level or slightly distant observation.

anchors.name: Landscape allowed to breathe, not postcard spectacle
anchors.concrete_expression: Landscape is allowed to breathe in a spacious frame with clean visual paths, anchored by a specific human action or detail (conversation, work, waiting, grief, play, bureaucracy, prayer, music or sport) so it does not become tourism or postcard spectacle.

anchors.name: Violence remains distant, viewer as witness
anchors.concrete_expression: Violence may remain distant, making the viewer witness rather than consume it.

anchors.name: Natural light carries the image
anchors.concrete_expression: Natural late-afternoon, desert, courtyard, sea or town light often carries the image: natural sun, dusk or shade with pale earth, sky, sand, water, white cloth, modest saturated accents and real environmental contrast.

anchors.name: Minimal camera intervention
anchors.concrete_expression: Minimal camera intervention encourages observation: patient eye-level or slightly distant observation, no aggressive lens intrusion, important action happening within the frame rather than the camera forcing toward it.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Violence remains distant, viewer as witness
uncheckable_by_design.reason: The anchor is conditional ('Violence may remain distant') and applies only when violence is depicted; a prompt with no violence cannot encode it, and witness-rather-than-consume is a viewer-effect judgment, not a token-expressible prompt property. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

CIS-35.micro_rules_source: No numeric micro-rule is stated in this profile (checked in full, lines 3933-4039); no value invented.
CIS-35.vocabularies_note: This profile supplies no closed framing-device, macro-narrative-object or light-source vocabulary of the kinds extracted for other profiles; its Composition list (line 3953) and Lighting/color list (line 3959) are open scene examples, not closed vocabularies, so none is recorded.

spacious framing.text: 'Create spacious frames with clean visual paths'; 'Use spacious, patient frames that invite the viewer into a place without visually possessing it.'
spacious framing.source: section 35, Composition, line 3953, and AI Deployment Block, line 3972

anchors.name: Normal houses and suburbs must first feel credible
anchors.concrete_expression: Normal houses and suburbs first feel credible: clean, ordinary suburban or institutional photography with believable home lighting, lawns, kitchens, bedrooms, schools, streets, phones, televisions and cars, per the Base reality rule, line 4060.

anchors.name: Dream/reality boundaries may be visually obvious in some moments and invisible in others
anchors.concrete_expression: Dream/reality boundaries may be visually obvious in some moments and invisible in others; some dream images remain photographically ordinary so reality cannot be trusted.

anchors.name: Boiler rooms, basements, hallways, stairs, bedrooms, windows, bathrooms, and school corridors become threat geometry
anchors.concrete_expression: Boiler rooms, basements, hallways, stairs, bedrooms, windows, bathrooms and school corridors become threat geometry: ordinary domestic architecture arranged as a trap, with doorway, window, closet, stair landing, phone-distance or stalking perspective making the space feel watched, per the POV rule, line 4069.

anchors.name: Red/green or warm/cool accents can operate as recognizable tension anchors
anchors.concrete_expression: Red/green or warm/cool accents operate as recognizable tension anchors: high contrast, steam, sodium orange, deep blue, industrial backlight or red/green punctuation reserved for heightened zones while waking scenes stay relatively natural, per the Lighting rule, line 4066.

anchors.name: Practical fog/steam belongs to industrial or dream environments, not everywhere
anchors.concrete_expression: Practical fog/steam belongs to industrial or dream environments only: steam emerging where it should not, inside boiler or industrial geometry, and never spread across ordinary waking scenes.

micro_rules_source.spatial_rule_violations: section 36, AI Deployment Block, line 4079: 'then violate exactly one spatial rule'; Breach rule, line 4063: 'Introduce one impossible spatial clue: corridor too long, doorway opening into wrong place, shadow behaving incorrectly, bathtub/bed threshold, stair geometry, figure in background, steam emerging where it should not.'

avoid.text: neon slasher color without location logic
overt monsters before spatial tension exists
surreal distortion that announces 'dream' immediately every time

CIS-36.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 4040-4146).

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Dream/reality boundaries may be visually obvious in some moments and invisible in others
uncheckable_by_design.reason: The alternation between an obvious and an invisible boundary is a property across moments and across a body of images; a single still is in one state or the other, so no prompt token can verify the alternation as written. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Practical fog/steam belongs to industrial or dream environments, not everywhere
uncheckable_by_design.reason: The per-image half is encoded (steam confined to an industrial or dream zone), but 'not everywhere' is a distribution property across a set of images, not a property one still can evidence. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.name: Ocean, horizon, wind, and humidity carry emotional meaning
anchors.concrete_expression: Ocean, horizon, wind and humidity carry emotional meaning: sea horizon, fabric moving in wind, reflective water and salt air made emotionally active but never postcard-pretty, per the Environment rule, lines 4167-4168.

anchors.name: Social/economic reality remains legible beneath the supernatural
anchors.concrete_expression: Social/economic reality remains legible beneath the supernatural: coastlines, unfinished towers, construction, streets, labor, bodies and economic absence stay readable while haunting emerges inside the same photographic reality.

anchors.name: Daylight can feel hot, pale, unfinished, and materially specific
anchors.concrete_expression: Daylight feels hot, pale, unfinished and materially specific: hot natural sun, pale concrete, blue sea, dust, sweat and bright sky, per the Day/night contrast rule, line 4170.

anchors.name: Night may become cool, neon, moonlit, or dreamlike without losing physical texture
anchors.concrete_expression: Night becomes cool, neon, moonlit or dreamlike without losing physical texture: cool blue/cyan, selective neon or practical color, dark skin with controlled highlights, moon and reflection, black negative space, per the Day/night contrast rule, line 4170.

anchors.name: Faces and skin remain luminous inside dark environments
anchors.concrete_expression: Faces and skin remain luminous inside dark environments: reflective skin and real material texture preserved, with controlled highlights on dark skin at night.

CIS-37.micro_rules_source: No numeric micro-rule is stated in this profile (checked in full, lines 4147-4250); the Supernatural rule, line 4173, is an ordering rule (change gaze, stillness, group behavior, reflection, eye light, repeated position, or temporal feeling before adding any overt effect), not a count, so no value is recorded. No value invented.

avoid.text: supernatural figures detached from social context

CIS-37.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 4147-4250). Black negative space appears only as one night-lighting element in the Day/night contrast rule; it is not mandated as sparse negative space composition.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Ocean, horizon, wind, and humidity carry emotional meaning
uncheckable_by_design.reason: The visible carriers are encoded (sea horizon, wind, humidity, salt air), but that they 'carry emotional meaning' is an emotional-quality criterion a viewer judges; no token can evidence the meaning itself. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.name: Gaze is a structural element
anchors.concrete_expression: Gaze is a structural element: watcher, watched, reflected, recorded or imagined, and it is clear who can see whom.

anchors.name: Architecture provides nested frames
anchors.concrete_expression: Architecture provides nested frames: doors, screens, windows, mirrors, railings, stairs and corridors, with at least two framing devices from the profile's closed vocabulary in the prompt.

anchors.name: Elegant, motivated camera movement translated to stills
anchors.concrete_expression: Camera movement is elegant and motivated, often revealing new spatial information, translated to a still as: a foreground object partially hides a face, a reflection reveals a second figure, a corridor creates a visual path, or a hand/object detail leads toward the main subject. Translation per this profile's Movement translated to stills rule, lines 4273-4274.

anchors.name: Macro details carry sensual/narrative weight
anchors.concrete_expression: Macro details of objects, hands, fabric, food, wounds, tools or writing carry sensual/narrative weight, and one macro-scale narrative object from the profile's closed vocabulary should matter.

anchors.name: Symmetry disturbed by an off-axis element
anchors.concrete_expression: Symmetry and meticulous design can be disturbed by an off-axis element expressing desire or threat.

micro_rules_source.framing_devices_min: section 38, Composition, line 4271: 'Include at least two of: mirror, glass, doorway, screen, banister, window, curtain, photograph, phone, telescope, camera, shadow, framed opening.'
micro_rules_source.macro_narrative_object_count: section 38, Detail, line 4280: 'One macro-scale narrative object should matter.'

avoid.text: color that does not belong to the set/materials

CIS-38.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 4251-4357). Symmetry is mandated, but centered composition as such is not stated.

anchors.name: Ancestry is present in bodies, landscape, ritual, memory, and material culture rather than as ghost decoration
anchors.concrete_expression: Ancestry is present in bodies, landscape, ritual, memory and material culture rather than as ghost decoration: family bodies in coastal place, ritual objects, indigo cloth, baskets, food, hair and hands carrying ancestry as lived material culture, never as supernatural effects.

anchors.name: Coastal landscape and natural light create a temporal continuum
anchors.concrete_expression: Coastal landscape and natural light create a temporal continuum: low-country/coastal horizon, luminous natural daylight, shade under trees and porches, late sun and reflected water layering historical and present time in one frame, per the Lighting rule, lines 4381-4382.

anchors.name: Black skin, white cloth, indigo, earth, green, sea, and food create rich material contrast
anchors.concrete_expression: Black skin, white cloth, indigo, earth, green, sea and food create rich material contrast: material color only, indigo cloth, off-white cotton, skin, green vegetation, brown earth, sea blue, food and weathered wood, per the Color rule, line 4384.

anchors.name: Group tableaux emphasize women, family, and generational relation
anchors.concrete_expression: Group tableaux emphasize women, family and generational relation: wide family tableaux, women in relation to landscape, repeated generations gathered at porches, fields, shorelines or tables, per the Composition rule, lines 4378-4379.

anchors.name: Slow motion or altered motion can shift ordinary action into ancestral/meditative time
anchors.concrete_expression: Slowed or layered time in a still, per this profile's Time in a still rule, line 4387: wind-caught fabric, suspended gesture, repeated generations, reflections, or a figure separated from normal motion, creating meditative ancestral time.

CIS-39.micro_rules_source: No numeric micro-rule is stated in this profile (checked in full, lines 4358-4464); no value invented.
CIS-39.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 4358-4464). Wide family tableaux are mandated by the Composition rule, but spacious framing as such is not stated; on the CIS-35 precedent, wide framing alone does not declare spacious framing.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Coastal landscape and natural light create a temporal continuum
uncheckable_by_design.reason: The carriers are encoded (coastal landscape, natural light, layered-time devices), but a 'temporal continuum' is an abstract temporal property spanning past and present; a single still can suggest it, not evidence it. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Slow motion or altered motion can shift ordinary action into ancestral/meditative time
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Slow or altered motion is a motion property; the profile's Time in a still rule (line 4387) supplies still substitutes, which are encoded, but the motion itself and the meditative time it creates cannot be verified from a still or its prompt tokens. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.name: Architecture can bend, lean, spike, curl, loom, or huddle like a character
anchors.concrete_expression: Architecture bends, leans, spikes, curls, looms or huddles like a character: distorted, intentionally designed buildings whose shapes comment on the outsider, per the Composition rule, line 4488.

anchors.name: Silhouette is highly important: pale face/dark costume, bare tree/fog, black roof/snow, tall narrow figure/rounded environment
anchors.concrete_expression: Silhouette is highly important: pale face against dark costume, bare tree in fog, black roof against snow, or a tall narrow figure against a rounded environment, with strong silhouette and frontal storybook readability, per the Composition rule, line 4488.

anchors.name: Palettes are limited and seasonal, often black/white/gray/brown with selective candy, red, blue, or green accents
anchors.concrete_expression: Palettes are limited and seasonal: a desaturated or near-monochrome world of black, white, gray and brown, restricted heavily, with one small family of heightened accents (candy, red, blue or green) when useful, per the Color rule, line 4494.

anchors.name: Backlit fog, snow, rain, smoke, moonlight, or diffuse sky create graphic depth
anchors.concrete_expression: Backlit fog, snow, rain, smoke, moonlight or diffuse sky create graphic depth: diffuse overcast, moonlike backlight, practical pools, snow bounce, fireplace light, or theatrical shafts through fog, with faces readable against dark costume and environment, per the Lighting rule, lines 4491-4492.

anchors.name: Sets feel handmade/theatrical rather than invisible naturalism
anchors.concrete_expression: Sets feel handmade and theatrical rather than invisible naturalism: an intentionally designed dark storybook world of handmade materials and controlled fog and weather, never glossy or casually real.

micro_rules_source.shape_motif_count: section 40, Shape language, line 4485: 'Choose 2-3 dominant shape motifs: crooked verticals, needle peaks, spirals, scallops, oversized circles, narrow windows, striped forms. Repeat across architecture, furniture, trees, costume, and props.' The Deployment Block, line 4504, repeats the band: buildings, trees, furniture, costume and props echo 2-3 shapes.

avoid.text: random crooked shapes with no repeated motif
photoreal naturalism that neutralizes the theatrical world

trait_source.centered composition: section 40, AI Deployment Block, line 4504: 'Center the outsider sympathetically within an environment that exaggerates difference.'

CIS-40.declared_traits_note: Centered composition is declared on the Deployment Block's explicit imperative 'Center the outsider sympathetically' (line 4504), the governing summary of this profile. Tension recorded, not smoothed: the Composition rule itself (line 4488) mandates 'strong silhouette and frontal storybook readability' and does not use the word centered; frontal staging alone would not declare the trait (CIS-25 precedent), and symmetry alone would not either (CIS-38 precedent). The declaration rests solely on the Deployment Block's own centering mandate (checked in full, lines 4465-4571). No other declarable trait is mandated: no spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is stated.

anchors.name: Real streets, markets, coast, roads, animals, vehicles, and bodies remain materially present
anchors.concrete_expression: Real streets, markets, coast, roads, animals, vehicles and bodies remain materially present: a real social environment photographed first, street, market, road, beach, bus, motorcycle, crowd, courtyard, shop or dusty open space, with hard sun, ordinary clothing, surface wear and uncontrolled life at the edges, per the Base reality rule, lines 4592-4593.

anchors.name: Symbolic imagery may interrupt realism without explanation
anchors.concrete_expression: Symbolic imagery interrupts realism without explanation: one concrete symbolic intrusion belonging to the character's desire or social reality, kept concrete rather than vaporous, per the Surreal collision rule, line 4595.

anchors.name: Montage can be jagged, associative, manic, or suddenly meditative
anchors.concrete_expression: Montage can be jagged, associative, manic, or suddenly meditative.

anchors.name: Strong color and sun can coexist with rough documentary texture
anchors.concrete_expression: Strong color and sun coexist with rough documentary texture: sun-struck color, grain, dust, skin, painted metal, fabric, sea, asphalt and urban signage, never smoothed into digital cleanliness, per the Color/texture rule, lines 4601-4602.

anchors.name: Repetition of vehicles, horns, animals, money, clothing, or urban signs can become rhythmic motifs
anchors.concrete_expression: Repetition of vehicles, horns, animals, money, clothing or urban signs becomes rhythmic motifs inside the frame: a named motif from the profile's closed vocabulary repeated so its rhythm is visible in the composition.
