seamless montage logic that removes the productive collision

CIS-41.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 4572-4678). The Composition rule mandates bold diagonals and asymmetry, the opposite pole from centered composition.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Montage can be jagged, associative, manic, or suddenly meditative
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Montage is an editing property across frames; a single still can carry the jagged symbolic collision (encoded under anchor 2 and the symbolic collision micro-rule) but cannot encode montage itself or its swings between manic and meditative rhythm. The profile states no movement-to-stills translation for montage. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.name: Events unfold in continuous space rather than being reduced to coverage fragments
anchors.concrete_expression: The image is constructed as a slice of continuous lived space: meaningful foreground and background action that feels capable of continuing beyond the frame, per the AI Deployment Block, line 4718.

anchors.name: Foreground, middle ground, and background may all contain meaningful action
anchors.concrete_expression: Foreground, middle ground and background all contain meaningful action: the subject placed in relation to an active environment with meaningful secondary action that would continue even if the protagonist left, per the Composition rule, line 4699.

anchors.name: Camera distance can change inside one conceptual shot
anchors.concrete_expression: A wide composition capable of becoming intimate through proximity, at eye-level or shoulder-height immersion with the viewer physically inside the scene, per the Camera rule, line 4702; the still carries the wide-to-intimate composition, not the change itself.

anchors.name: Natural/available or environment-driven light supports realism
anchors.concrete_expression: Natural, available or environment-driven light supports realism: overcast sky, windows, practical lamps, car light, fire, street sources or sun through haze, with no obviously separate key/fill/rim construction, per the Lighting rule, line 4705.

anchors.name: Long-lens voyeurism is less important than embodied spatial presence
anchors.concrete_expression: Embodied spatial presence replaces long-lens voyeurism: the viewer occupies the street, room, car, crowd, beach or crisis at eye or shoulder level rather than observing from a detached telephoto position, per the AI Deployment Block, line 4718.

micro_rules_source.depth_planes_min: section 42, Composition, line 4699: 'Build a frame with at least three spatial planes.' The Deployment Block, line 4718, restates it as 'three readable depth planes.'

avoid.text: conventional hero close-up disconnected from the event
montage-like visual clutter in one still

CIS-42.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 4679-4785). Wide compositions are mandated, but spacious framing as such is not stated; on the CIS-35 precedent, wide framing alone does not declare it.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Events unfold in continuous space rather than being reduced to coverage fragments
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Unfolding is a duration property; the Deployment Block's still form (a slice of continuous lived space with action continuing beyond the frame) is encoded, but the event's continuation in time cannot be verified from one still or its prompt tokens. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Camera distance can change inside one conceptual shot
uncheckable_by_design.reason: A change of camera distance inside one shot is a motion property; a still holds exactly one distance. The Camera rule's still residue (wide composition capable of becoming intimate through proximity) is encoded, but the change itself is uncheckable by design. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.concrete_expression: Frame the person as a full psychological subject whose face is held long enough to communicate thought: eyes, jaw, posture, hands and stillness carry moral weight, at a respectful camera distance with non-exploitative framing, so the person reads as a person first and never as a symbol of a cause. Translation of 'dignity' per section 0A lines 111-112, applied with this profile's Portraiture rule, line 4811.
anchors.name: The human subject is never merely an illustration of an issue

anchors.concrete_expression: Build the institutional zone from controlled lines, doors, glass, desks, hallways and partitions with uniform spacing and centered or slightly boxed-in figures, lit by restrained neutral/cool practical light at low saturation with controlled contrast, so the space itself reads still, repetitive and draining. Per this profile's Composition and Lighting/color rules, lines 4805 and 4808.
anchors.name: Institutional spaces can be still, repetitive, compressed, and emotionally draining

anchors.concrete_expression: Open the frame for community and private life: relationships in view, patterned clothing, shop and home detail, street life and brighter spatial depth, with richer wardrobe and environmental color, warmer skin and daylight or household practicals. Per this profile's Composition and Lighting/color rules, lines 4805 and 4808.
anchors.name: Community and private life can be richer in color, texture, and movement

anchors.concrete_expression: Use a held, purposeful close-up: the face stays in frame long enough to communicate thought, with eyes, jaw, posture, hands and stillness carrying the moral weight and no melodramatic expression. Per this profile's Portraiture rule, line 4811.
anchors.name: Close-ups are purposeful and emotionally patient

anchors.concrete_expression: Populate historical Black life with beauty, fashion, home, commerce, family and ordinary pleasure alongside gravity: dressed figures, a lived-in home interior, a shop or market transaction, a family grouping and a moment of everyday enjoyment, in vibrant but historically credible color. Per this profile's invariants, lines 4795-4801, and Lighting/color rule, line 4808.
anchors.name: Historical Black life should contain beauty, fashion, home, commerce, family, and ordinary pleasure, not only suffering

CIS-43.micro_rules_source: No numeric micro-rule is stated in this profile (checked in full, lines 4786-4888); no value invented.

avoid.text: gray desaturation for every historical scene
reducing community scenes to background color without individual people

CIS-43.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 4786-4888). Centered figures appear only as one alternative ('centered or slightly boxed-in') inside the institutional-zone treatment, while the community treatment opens the frame, so centered composition as such is not mandated (Composition, line 4805).

anchors.concrete_expression: The environment is fully built before styling: a dense, tactile production design of named materials and constructed detail fills foreground, midground and background, so the world itself carries the image rather than decorating it. Per this profile's World first and Composition rules, lines 4909 and 4918.
anchors.name: Production design carries enormous visual responsibility

anchors.concrete_expression: One atmosphere justified by the location (rain in a street or industrial city, dust in a desert or battlefield, steam around machinery, smoke near fire, condensation in a sealed interior) hangs in the air and catches the directional light, making the light's direction and shafts visible. Per this profile's Atmosphere rule, line 4912.
anchors.name: Atmosphere makes light visible: smoke, rain, dust, steam, mist, sand, snow, condensation

anchors.concrete_expression: Strong backlight or directional shafts cut through the layered environment, carving foreground, subject and background into depth and preserving silhouettes against the light. Per this profile's Lighting rule, line 4915.
anchors.name: Strong backlight or directional shafts carve depth through complex environments

anchors.concrete_expression: Foreground objects (doorways, machinery, columns, crowd elements or structures) layer in front of the subject with the large environment behind it, creating visual density across the depth planes. Per this profile's Composition rule, line 4918.
anchors.name: Foreground layers create visual density

anchors.concrete_expression: A low camera position looks up at the structure, machine, crowd or warrior so it looms with physical weight and mass against the environment and sky. Per this profile's Composition rule, line 4918, and invariants, line 4902.
anchors.name: Low camera positions often give structures, machines, crowds, or warriors physical weight

micro_rules_source.material_family_count_min: section 44, World first, line 4909: 'Build at least three material families into the environment.'

avoid.text: light that does not interact with weather/material
production design reduced to background wallpaper

CIS-44.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 4889-4997). Widescreen staging preserves environment and scale but is not stated as a uniform-ratio mandate.

anchors.concrete_expression: A spare, readable composition in a simple room, courtyard, street, workshop or open landscape with competing objects limited, so the subject and the distances between people stay emotionally legible. Per this profile's Composition rule, line 5018.
anchors.name: Composition is spare and readable rather than crowded

anchors.concrete_expression: Warm local color (ochre, yellow, orange, earth, dark blue/black, skin, cloth, painted walls) is vivid but tied to actual location materials, with small saturated accents grounded in place and no global orange grade. Per this profile's Color rule, line 5024.
anchors.name: Warm local color — ochre, yellow, orange, earth — can be vivid without becoming a tourist filter

anchors.concrete_expression: In a night scene, the darkness stays deep and dense while one strong practical or directional source models faces and hands in a controlled pool of light, with Caravaggio-like contrast held below theatrical excess. Per this profile's Lighting rule, line 5021.
anchors.name: Night may be deep and dense, with faces emerging through controlled pools of light

anchors.concrete_expression: A fixed or patient wide frame holds the subject at a dignified distance in the spare composition, letting posture, distance and light carry the narrative rather than camera movement or close intrusion. Per this profile's invariants, line 5010, and Composition rule, line 5018.
anchors.name: Fixed or patient wide framing supports dignity

anchors.concrete_expression: One ordinary object (fan, motorcycle, uniform, chair, water container, phone, fabric or tool) is chosen and its presence repeated within the scene and its context, so the object accrues emotional or social meaning. Per this profile's Object rule, line 5027.
anchors.name: Everyday objects can become visual metaphors through repetition and context

micro_rules_source.ordinary_object_count: section 45, Object rule, line 5027: 'Choose one ordinary object — fan, motorcycle, uniform, chair, water container, phone, fabric, tool — and let its repeated presence carry emotion or social meaning.'

CIS-45.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 4998-5104). Spare, uncluttered composition and fixed or patient wide framing are mandated, but neither 'spacious framing' nor 'sparse negative space' is stated as such.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Night may be deep and dense, with faces emerging through controlled pools of light
uncheckable_by_design.reason: The anchor is conditional ('Night may be...') and applies only when the image is a night scene; a daylight prompt cannot encode it. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Everyday objects can become visual metaphors through repetition and context
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Repetition across context and the metaphorical reading are sequence/reception properties: a single still can show the chosen object and its within-frame repetition, but whether it reads as a visual metaphor is a viewer judgment no token can settle. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.concrete_expression: The landscape is staged as an active force on the figure: a vast mountain, wet forest, beach or bright field presses in, looms or opens around the body so the environment visibly weighs on, threatens or releases the character rather than decorating the scene. Per this profile's Composition rule, line 5125, and invariants, line 5114.
anchors.name: Landscape operates as psychological pressure, desire, threat, freedom, or secrecy

anchors.concrete_expression: One tactile human detail (a hand gripping leather, mud on a skirt, hair blowing across a face, fingers on fabric, a crushed flower) is paired with the environmental force and rendered in close, sensual material detail so the detail carries the character's inner state. Per this profile's Composition rule, line 5125.
anchors.name: Tactile details of bodies and materials carry interior emotion

anchors.concrete_expression: Use a partial or fragmented point of view (partial POV, shoulder view, hand/body detail or intimate close-up) instead of conventional frontal portraiture, so the scene is seen from inside the subject's experience. Per this profile's Camera rule, line 5128.
anchors.name: Female or otherwise intimate subjectivity can be expressed through partial/fragmented point of view

anchors.concrete_expression: Weather and terrain visibly act on the body: wind drives hair and grass, mud marks skin and clothing, water soaks fabric, mountain scale dwarfs or shelters the figure. Per this profile's invariants, line 5117, and Composition rule, line 5125.
anchors.name: Nature is not merely scenic; weather, mud, grass, water, mountains, and wind act on bodies

anchors.concrete_expression: Use real sun, cloud, fog, window, fire or dawn/dusk light with its uneven illumination accepted (weather-softened, partially shadowed, odd in falloff) so nature feels present rather than polished. Per this profile's Lighting rule, line 5131.
anchors.name: Natural light is allowed to be imperfect or odd

micro_rules_source.environmental_force_count: section 46, Composition, line 5125: 'Pair one environmental force with one tactile human detail.'
micro_rules_source.tactile_human_detail_count: section 46, Composition, line 5125: 'Pair one environmental force with one tactile human detail.'

avoid.text: tactile close-ups with no emotional connection

CIS-46.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 5105-5211). The wide-landscape and bodily-close-detail pairing is a scale contrast, not a spacious-framing mandate as stated.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Landscape operates as psychological pressure, desire, threat, freedom, or secrecy
uncheckable_by_design.reason: The landscape's psychological function (pressure, desire, threat, freedom or secrecy) is an interpretive property of the image's inner meaning; a still can encode the landscape physically dominating or releasing the figure, but which psychological role it plays is residual judgment. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.concrete_expression: Place an archival image and a contemporary image in visible juxtaposition inside one frame (photograph-in-scene, projection, split temporal echo, portrait beside document) with their material textures kept distinct, so past and present face each other. Per this profile's Composition rule, line 5235, and Evidence layers rule, line 5232.
anchors.name: Archival image and contemporary image are placed in argument with each other

anchors.concrete_expression: Make one record medium the image's evidence: a photograph, television frame, document, newspaper, map or public monument is physically present and legible in the scene, carrying the historical claim. Per this profile's invariants, line 5222.
anchors.name: Photographs, television frames, documents, newspapers, speeches, maps, or public monuments can become visual evidence

anchors.concrete_expression: Keep each medium's native texture (silver-grain still, faded print, broadcast scanlines/softness, 16mm grain, modern digital clarity) unhomogenized: no single grade flattens the eras into one look. Per this profile's Texture rule, line 5238.
anchors.name: Historical material retains its native texture instead of being cosmetically modernized

anchors.concrete_expression: Where a reenacted scene is used, it sits visibly beside the genuine archival material as a restrained, clearly staged layer that clarifies the record, its texture distinct from the evidence it interprets. Per this profile's Evidence layers rule, line 5232, and invariants, line 5224.
anchors.name: Reenactment should clarify history, not pretend to replace evidence

anchors.concrete_expression: Compose public space, crowd, institution, portrait and archive into one structural relation (a crowd before a monument with an archival photograph present, a portrait beside its document in a courtroom, parliament or street), anchored to faces, bodies, labor or testimony. Per this profile's Composition rule, line 5235, and Human rule, line 5241.
anchors.name: Public space, crowd, institution, portrait, and archive are connected structurally

micro_rules_source.evidence_layer_count: section 47, Evidence layers, line 5232: 'Choose 2-3 temporal materials: archival black-and-white still, 16mm/newsreel frame, television image, typed document, contemporary color photograph, reenacted scene.' Deployment block, line 5251, confirms the same count: 'Combine 2-3 materially distinct evidence layers'.

avoid.text: glossy reenactment pretending to be original footage
flattening all eras into one color grade

CIS-47.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 5212-5318).

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Reenactment should clarify history, not pretend to replace evidence
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Whether a reenactment 'pretends to replace evidence' is an epistemic honesty property of the maker's claim, not a visible property of the still; the encodable half (a visibly staged, texture-distinct reenacted layer beside genuine archival material) is carried in the anchor record. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.concrete_expression: Let one emotionally charged detail (a hand on a sink, a shoe in a hallway, an empty chair, bruised knuckles, torn fabric) carry the story information by itself, with no explanatory wide shot of the whole event. Per this profile's Fragment rule, line 5339.
anchors.name: Detail can replace exposition

anchors.concrete_expression: Keep the violent or major act itself outside the frame and show its charged remainder (a stain, a reflection, blood diluted in water, a curtain still moving), with the offscreen space felt as active pressure at the frame's edges. Per this profile's Composition rule, line 5342, and invariants, line 5329.
anchors.name: Violence or major action may remain partly or entirely offscreen

anchors.concrete_expression: Center an object, body fragment or texture (hand, stain, curtain, shoe, food, reflection, water, bruised skin, torn fabric) rendered with precise tactile light, so the fragment is the scene's emotional evidence. Per this profile's Fragment rule, line 5339, and deployment block, line 5358.
anchors.name: Objects, body fragments, and textures carry memory and guilt

anchors.concrete_expression: Withhold the connecting explanation: cropped bodies, partial rooms and an isolated charged fragment are left for the viewer to connect, with the frame's photographic precision intact and the narrative deliberately incomplete. Per this profile's Composition rule, line 5342, and invariants, line 5331.
anchors.name: Ellipsis creates emotional participation: the viewer must connect fragments

anchors.concrete_expression: Freeze an ordinary action at a suspended, mid-gesture instant (a hand half-raised, a curtain still swinging, fabric caught mid-fall) so the held gesture reads uncanny or lyrical rather than documentary. Per this profile's invariants, line 5332.
anchors.name: Slow motion or suspended gesture can make ordinary action uncanny or lyrical

micro_rules_source.persistent_color_signal_count: section 48, Color, line 5345: 'Choose one persistent color signal only when story-relevant — red, yellow, blue, green — and let it recur in object/material form rather than global grading.' The count applies under the rule's own story-relevant condition.

avoid.text: explaining the entire narrative in one frame
dreamy blur used as a substitute for memory

CIS-48.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 5319-5425). Negative space appears only as one composition option among several ('or a still object surrounded by negative space', Composition, line 5342), not as a mandate.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Violence or major action may remain partly or entirely offscreen
uncheckable_by_design.reason: The anchor is conditional ('may remain') and its content is an absence: the act is defined by not being shown. A still can encode the aftermath fragment and active offscreen pressure, but the withheld event itself cannot be token-verified. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Objects, body fragments, and textures carry memory and guilt
uncheckable_by_design.reason: That an object or fragment 'carries memory and guilt' is an emotional-quality property: the charged object and its tactile rendering are encodable, but the memory and guilt it carries are viewer-side judgments. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

uncheckable_by_design.anchor: Ellipsis creates emotional participation: the viewer must connect fragments
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Emotional participation is a reception property: the viewer connecting the fragments happens in the viewer, not in the frame. The encodable half (withheld explanation, unconnected fragments) is carried in the anchor record. Residual judgment per FIX-PLAN B6.

anchors.concrete_expression: Frame the community, not a glamour center: several people occupy a patient wide or medium-wide frame in functional relation (a village meeting, schoolyard, clinic, courtyard gathering), with no single figure glamorized above the social system. Per this profile's Composition rule, line 5446.
anchors.name: Community and social systems are more important than individual glamour

anchors.concrete_expression: Give the natural environment autonomous presence: rain, forest canopy, mud, open sky or road occupies real material weight in the frame and is allowed to dominate when appropriate, not serve as backdrop. Per this profile's Environment rule, line 5449.
anchors.name: Natural environment — forest, rain, earth, courtyard, road, village — has autonomous presence

anchors.concrete_expression: Hold a simple, patient frame in which the weather and the collective behavior (rain falling on a schoolyard, a crowd waiting, communal work) are themselves the event of the image. Per this profile's invariants, line 5437, and Composition rule, line 5446.
anchors.name: Simple, patient frames can let weather and collective behavior become the event

anchors.concrete_expression: Stage the image in a civic space (school, clinic, village meeting, home, road or institution) where the social action of the community plays out, with local architecture and material detail giving it real presence. Per this profile's Composition rule, line 5446.
anchors.name: Schools, clinics, village meetings, homes, roads, and institutions become civic stages

anchors.concrete_expression: Arrange the frame per the Perspective rule: when an outsider or institutional power appears, do not make them the heroic visual center; keep community reaction, local interpretation and the surrounding social system visible around them. Per this profile's Perspective rule, line 5455.
anchors.name: The point of view resists colonial hero framing and centers African social interpretation

CIS-49.micro_rules_source: No numeric micro-rule is stated in this profile (checked in full, lines 5426-5534); 'several people' in the Composition rule is not a structured count, so no value was invented from it.

avoid.text: invented technical claims unsupported by the films

CIS-49.declared_traits_note: None of centered composition, spacious framing, sparse negative space or uniform ratio is mandated by this profile (checked in full, lines 5426-5534). Patient wide or medium-wide community framing is mandated, but 'spacious framing' is not stated as such.

anchors.name: Faces are primary landscapes
anchors.concrete_expression: The human face is the primary landscape: close or extreme-close portraiture moved close enough that tiny facial changes matter, preserving skin texture, eye moisture, wrinkles and asymmetry.

anchors.name: Extreme or very close two-face compositions
anchors.concrete_expression: Extreme or very close two-face compositions can collapse personal boundaries: full face, profile, overlapping faces, face beside face, or one face emerging from shadow.

anchors.name: Window/natural light reveals the face
anchors.concrete_expression: Window/natural light reveals skin, eyes, age, fatigue and emotional contradiction: soft window light, overcast daylight, single practical lamp, candle or a severe directional source.

anchors.name: Sparse interiors and negative space
anchors.concrete_expression: Sparse interiors and negative space prevent distraction from psychology: a simplified room (bed, wall, curtain, doorway, chair, table, window or bare landscape) where negative space and stillness concentrate the face.

anchors.name: High-contrast black-and-white or controlled symbolic color
anchors.concrete_expression: High-contrast black-and-white or controlled symbolic color are both valid: for black-and-white protect luminous midtones and deep but readable blacks; for color choose a severe symbolic field such as crimson/white/black rather than many competing hues.

CIS-50.micro_rules_source: No numeric micro-rule is stated in this profile (checked in full, lines 5535-5640); the crimson/white/black field at line 5558 is given as an example ('such as'), not as a color-count rule, so no count was invented from it.

avoid.text: ornate set decoration that competes with faces
melodramatic crying as a shortcut for depth

sparse negative space.text: 'Sparse interiors and negative space prevent distraction from psychology'; 'Let negative space and stillness concentrate the face.'
sparse negative space.source: section 50, Five non-negotiable visual anchors, anchor 4, lines 5579-5584, and Composition, line 5561
